key_insight: Simple local quantum processes can match high-order moments of random unitaries while still remaining efficiently distinguishable from truly random behavior.
engineering_relevance: For quantum algorithm design and scrambling models, unitary designs alone may be insufficient as a proxy for pseudorandomness or secure randomness generation.
method: Builds families of efficiently samplable 1- and 2-qubit gate distributions.
Composes them for T = O_t(n^2 log^2 n) steps to obtain approximate unitary t-designs.
Uses efficient quantum distinguishers to test pseudorandomness beyond moment matching.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximate unitary t-designs with negligible error exp(-Ω(log^2 n)) but an efficient distinguisher using only O_t(log^2 n) queries.
watch_item: Moment-matching guarantees can hide exploitable structure, so designs should not be assumed pseudorandom without separate indistinguishability tests.
paper_title: On the pseudorandomness of simple quantum processes
